title: Core Facilitator and Core GovOps hold full discretion both to find a security incident and to set its penalty
content:
A.1.10.2.3.2.2.1.3.3 states that "the Core Facilitator and Core GovOps, in consultation with other appropriate stakeholders, have **full discretion** to determine whether a Prime Spell Security Incident has occurred and to impose appropriate penalties."

The penalty list at A.1.10.2.3.2.2.1.3.4 is open-ended ("may include, without limitation") and materially severe: financial penalties, deprioritization in the Executive Spell queue, exclusion from an upcoming Executive Vote cycle, mandatory additional audits at the Prime's expense, and suspension of non-essential support from the Core Council or the Prime's Operational Executor Agent.

Exclusion from a vote cycle is the one worth dwelling on. A Prime Agent's ability to act on chain runs entirely through the Executive Process, so exclusion is a temporary suspension of the Prime's operational capacity — imposed at the discretion of process operators rather than by a governance vote.

Combined with the fact that the rules being enforced may exist only in a Slack channel (A.1.10.2.3.2.2.1.2), the same two parties effectively define, detect, judge and sentence. The chunk specifies no appeal, no evidentiary standard, and no escalation to SKY holders. In a document whose stated subject is the balance of powers, this is a deliberate and visible concentration of it — presented as an interim measure, which is exactly the framing the Atlas elsewhere warns produces Slippery Slope Misalignment.
description: Detection, adjudication and sentencing sit with the same two parties, with penalties reaching financial fines, queue deprioritization and exclusion from a vote cycle; no appeal route is specified.
